archetype.name: Rebuilding (run-and-gun)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a 31-51 season that plays at one of the league's fastest paces, hands heavy usage to its forwards, and has not yet shown a defense that can keep it in games.

report.headline: Bricked threes hide a familiar problem: this defense still can't stop anyone
report.take:
Chicago is 1-2, 25th of 30 on the site, and the numbers back that placement. The Net Rtg of -12.4 ranks 27th. The offense sits 25th and the defense 22nd. This is a team that runs, with a Pace of 107.6 against a league mean of 101.4. It hoists from deep at the seventh-highest 3PA Rate and lives at the line with the third-best FT Rate. It is also coming off a 31-51 season with a -5.1 Net Rtg, so a slow start is not news.

The headline number is the shooting. A 22.6 3P% ranks last in the league, 11.5 points under the league mean, and it drags the eFG % to 46, also last. That will not hold. The 3PA Rate of 44.9 is right in line with the last two seasons (45.7 and 44.3), when this same shot diet produced 3P% in the mid-30s. The scheme hasn't changed, and the makes will come back. The point guard play is a big part of the shortfall. Josh Giddey has a 30.6 TS % and a -29.2 On-Off while running the offense with 25 assists. Tre Jones, in fewer minutes, is at 60.1 TS % with a +36.2 On-Off. Caleb Wilson carries a 29.2 USG % at a 49.7 TS %, which is a lot of possessions spent below average.

The point differential flatters nobody but needs context. The 92-135 loss at Toronto accounts for more than the whole season's -40. The win at Milwaukee and the four-point home loss to Washington were essentially a wash, and the W vs Pt Diff of 0 says the record matches the play. The part that worries more is the defense. A DRtg of 118.9 is nearly identical to last season's 118.1. Opponents' wings are feasting, with small forwards scoring well over their own averages and taking an outsized share of points. The Opp TOV % of 11.8 ranks 25th, which echoes last year's 11.1. The offense should rise as the threes start falling. The defense looks like the same problem it was a year ago.

Expect the efficiency gap to close and the record to settle into the range the pace implies, a bottom-eight team rather than a bottom-three one. The free-throw surge is the likeliest piece to fade. The FT Rate was 24.6 last year against 38.8 now, so some of the offense's floor goes with it.

strengths.title: Living at the free-throw line
strengths.body: Chicago's FT Rate of 38.8 is third in the league and well above the league mean, and it has kept a cold-shooting offense from collapsing entirely. It is a big jump from last season's 24.6, so some of it is a three-game sample. Pace and an attacking style should keep it above average even if it fades.

strengths.title: Crashing the glass in transition
strengths.body: The Bulls rank seventh in RPG and above the league in ORB %. Some of that is the pace, since more possessions and more misses mean more boards. Still, a 29.1 ORB % is well above their recent seasons, and it has bought second chances that a 46 eFG % badly needs.

strengths.title: Tre Jones steadying the backcourt
strengths.body: Jones has the best individual line in a D- backcourt: 60.1 TS %, a positive BPM and a +36.2 On-Off. He ranks 24th on the point guard tab, well ahead of Giddey. If the minutes tilt toward him, the half-court offense should look less broken.

concerns.title: Same leaky defense as last year
concerns.body: The DRtg of 118.9 ranks 22nd and almost matches last season's 118.1, so this is not early noise. The defense forces few turnovers, with an Opp TOV % ranking 25th, which repeats a pattern from last year. Opposing small forwards are producing well beyond their own averages. Without stops or steals, the fast pace mostly gives opponents more possessions.

concerns.title: Point guard play sinking the offense
concerns.body: Giddey has played big minutes with a 30.6 TS % and a -29.2 On-Off. The backcourt grades D- overall. Some of his shooting will bounce back, but a lineup where the primary initiator can't score lets defenses load up on Wilson and Powell.

concerns.title: Usage concentrated in inefficient hands
concerns.body: Caleb Wilson leads the team in minutes and carries a 29.2 USG % at a 49.7 TS %, with a negative BPM. Volume without efficiency is a common early-season growing pain. Until it improves, the offense's ceiling stays low even after the threes regress up.

trend.note: Three games run from a 43-point loss at Toronto to a 132-125 win at Milwaukee and a four-point home loss. There is no stable baseline yet beyond a defense that looks like last season's.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, two in Boston, and a stingy Philly finish
weekAhead.body:
Four games, three of them away. Boston twice is the swing pairing. The Celtics' defense is barely better than Chicago's at DRtg 117.8, and they are 27th in REB %, which plays straight into the Bulls' offensive rebounding. The danger is the other end: Boston shoots 39.5 from three on a high 3PA Rate, and Chicago's perimeter defense hasn't shown it can contest that. The Knicks at home are the most winnable game. New York has the league's worst offense, but its 80.0 DRB % ranks second and will wipe out Chicago's second chances.

The week closes in Philadelphia against the strongest team on the schedule. The 76ers are 3-1 with a fifth-ranked DRtg of 102.5 and A-range grades in the backcourt and on the wings. Philly's REB % ranks last, though, so the glass is Chicago's lever there too. A split of the four would be a reasonable result. Winning more than two requires the three-ball to come back.

keyMatchups.title: Bulls' boards vs Boston's glass
keyMatchups.body: Boston ranks 27th in REB % and 29th in RPG, while Chicago is seventh in RPG. Across two games in Boston, extra possessions are how the Bulls offset the Celtics' shooting edge. That edge comes from pace and effort and should travel.

keyMatchups.title: Knicks' defensive glass at home
keyMatchups.body: New York's 108.6 DRtg ranks 10th and its 80.0 DRB % is second in the league, which takes away Chicago's offensive rebounds. The Knicks' 30th-ranked offense gives the Bulls' defense a rare soft target. This is the game to bank.

keyMatchups.title: Philadelphia's defense, last stop
keyMatchups.body: The 76ers own a fifth-ranked DRtg of 102.5 and the league's lowest TOV %. Chicago's defense won't get cheap turnovers from them, and its own shots will be contested. Philly's last-ranked REB % is the one opening.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the 3P % climbs off the league floor. On this shot diet, it decides every game.

restOfSeason.body:
The shooting will come up. A team taking this many threes with the same approach that hit in the mid-30s the last two seasons is not a 22.6 percent team. That alone should lift the offense toward the low-110s in ORtg, but some of the free-throw surge likely fades alongside it. The defense is the sticky part: it matches last year's, and the forced-turnover deficit has been there for two seasons. A defense like this caps the team in the bottom third even with average shooting.

The pace projects 27 wins. I'd put the range at 24 to 33, depending mostly on whether the defense improves at all and on how the backcourt minutes shake out between Giddey and Jones. Wilson's efficiency on heavy usage is the long-term variable worth tracking.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting regressing toward recent norms
Any defensive improvement on last season's DRtg
Backcourt minutes split between Giddey and Jones

confidence.note: Three games, one a 43-point outlier; history anchors the defense read.
